name: Beef Rendang

instructions.primary_message: Slice the shallots. Slice the garlic. Slice the ginger. Slice the galangal. Slice the turmeric. Slice the lemongrass. Slice the sirloin into half-inch chunks. Tie the turmeric leaf into knot. Tear the makrut lime leaves.
instructions.secondary_message:
10 shallots
4 cloves garlic
1 inch ginger
1 inch galangal
1 inch turmeric
2 stalks lemongrass
1 lb sirloin
1 turmeric leaf
2 makrut lime leaves

instructions.primary_message: Place coconut in wok over medium heat and dry-fry until golden brown. Cool slightly before grinding finely in mortar and pestle, or in food processor.

Snip chiles into 1-inch lengths. Soak in hot water until softened. Discard half the seeds and place the chiles in electric blender jug with shallots, garlic, ginger, galangal, turmeric and lemongrass. If you want a hotter rendang, add bird chiles. Add 1/2 cup water and grind to a paste- but not too finely.

Place spice paste, beef, coconut milk, and water in a roomy wok. Bring to a boil and simmer on medium heat, stirring now and then until mixture is well reduced and thick and oil surfaces—at least 45 minutes.

Add ground toasted coconut, turmeric leaf (if using), makrut lime leaf, salt, sugar, and asam keping (if using). Cook another 5-10 minutes, taste, and adjust seasonings if necessary. Take pan off heat. Serve with rice.

description: One of Malaysia's better-known dishes is beef rendang, a slow-cooked dry curry deeply spiced with ginger and tumeric, kaffir lime and chilis. In Malaysian fashion, it fuses sweet, sour, and savory elements.
notes: Optional or for serving: 4 to 6 bird chiles, optional
author: The Serious Eats Team
